q: The Sobolev embedding theorem relates Sobolev spaces W^{k,p}(Ω) to continuous function spaces. For p > n (dimension of domain), the embedding W^{1,p}(Ω) ↪ C^{0,α}(Ω) holds with α =
exp: Morrey's inequality: for p > n, W^{1,p}(Ω) ↪ C^{0,1−n/p}(Ω) (Hölder continuous with exponent α = 1−n/p). This allows Sobolev functions to be represented pointwise (not just a.e.) when p > n, which is crucial for regularity theory of PDEs.
